title: Split CI test topology and required check contract
description:
Problem: introducing browser tests into CI without clear topology can obscure failures and inflate runtime unpredictably.

Desired outcome: split CI into clear jobs (dotnet validation and browser validation) with stable check names and branch-protection alignment.

Scope:
- In scope: workflow restructuring, dependency caching strategy, explicit check naming, and branch protection guidance documentation.
- Out of scope: organization-wide branch protection automation.

Dependencies:
- Browser gate task TSK-0067.

Acceptance criteria:
- CI reports at least two explicit validation jobs with clear ownership of failures.
- Required checks are documented and consistent over time.
- Browser job failures do not suppress .NET test result visibility.

Validation:
- Run CI with both green and induced-failure scenarios to verify signal clarity.

Rollback:
- Keep split jobs but temporarily make browser job informational if severe flakiness emerges.

comments.author: AgentSmith
comments.body: Created from audit risk R-002 to keep CI signal quality high while adding browser gates.

comments.author: AgentSmith
comments.body: Completed by splitting CI into build-and-test and browser-navigation-freeze jobs. README validation guidance now documents the stable check names and ownership: build/test/coverage in build-and-test, Playwright navigation freeze and browser artifacts in browser-navigation-freeze.
